item.title: Roles
item.description:
A role is the unit you assign to people. It answers the question “what is this person here to do?” and translates that answer into permissions. Layer5 Cloud builds every role from the same three layers:

  • A key allows exactly one action, such as creating a team or approving a catalog request. See Keys.
  • A keychain bundles related keys, such as everything needed to manage teams. See Keychains.
  • A role bundles keychains.

A user’s permissions in an organization are the union of the keys from every role they hold in that organization. Holding two roles never removes anything; it only adds. The organization in context decides which roles count: the same person can administer one organization and hold only the User role in another, and their permissions differ accordingly. When a request names an organization, that organization is the context, even if the session points at a different one. Security Boundaries explains why the organization is an authorization boundary.

item.title: Permissions by Role
item.description:
This page tells you which Kanvas actions require a permission, which default roles grant each permission, and which actions are limited by something other than a permission. Use it to find out why an action is missing for a user and which role grants it.

How permissions work 🔗

A permission is a named key, such as Deploy Design, that allows one action. Keys are grouped into keychains, and a role bundles one or more keychains. Your organization assigns roles to users. Before Kanvas offers certain actions, it checks whether the user holds the matching key. Kanvas uses the shared Layer5 permission set and defines no permissions of its own. See Roles and Keychains.

item.title: Roles and Permissions
item.description:
This page tells you which permissions each default Layer5 Cloud role holds. Use it to find out why an action is missing for a user and which role grants it. For how roles, keychains, and permissions fit together, see Roles.

How permission checks work 🔗

A permission is a named key that allows one action, such as Create Team. A keychain groups keys, and a role groups keychains. Layer5 Cloud checks the key, never the role name. Before it runs a guarded action, Cloud resolves the organization the request names, then checks whether the user holds the key through a role in that organization. A user’s permissions are the union of the keys from every role the user holds there.
